The '''2019–20 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Cincinnati]] in the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Bearcats were led by first-year head-coach [[John Brannen (basketball)|John Brannen]]. The team played their home games at [[Fifth Third Arena]] as members of the [[American Athletic Conference]].

==Previous season==
The [[2018–19 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Bearcats]] finished the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]] 28–7, 14–4 in [[2018–19 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]], finishing in second place. They defeated [[2018–19 SMU Mustangs men's basketball team|SMU]], [[2018–19 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]], and No. 1 seed [[2018–19 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] to win the [[2019 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] for the second consecutive year, and received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 7 seed in the South region, they were upset by No. 10 seed [[2018–19 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] in the first round. After the conclusion of the NCAA tournament, head coach [[Mick Cronin (basketball)|Mick Cronin]] accepted the head-coaching position at [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Cronin leaves Cincinnati to take UCLA job |url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26478769/cronin-leaves-cincinnati-take-ucla-job |website=ESPN.com |date=9 April 2019 |access-date=9 April 2019}}</ref> [[John Brannen (basketball)|John Brannen]], the head coach at [[Cincinnati metropolitan area|nearby]] [[Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball|Northern Kentucky]], would be hired to replace Cronin.<ref>{{cite web |title=John Brannen Named Cincinnati Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2019/4/14/john-brannen-named-cincinnati-mens-basketball-coach.aspx |website=GoBearcats.com |access-date=14 April 2019}}</ref> In the transition, UC lost G/F Rashawn Fredericks and C Nysier Brooks - both of whom would've both been seniors. They also lost sophomore guard [[Logan Johnson]] and backup PF Eliel Nsoseme. Incoming freshman and [[Ohio Mr. Basketball|Ohio's Mr. Basketball]] in 2019, Samari Curtis, also de-committed. [[Jarron Cumberland]] announced he would test the waters to enter the [[2019 NBA draft]] on April 20, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fox19.com/2019/04/20/ucs-jarron-cumberland-will-test-nba-draft-waters/ |title=UC's Jarron Cumberland will test the NBA draft waters |last=Rauch |first=Jeremy |date=20 Apr 2019 |website=fox19.com |publisher=[[WXIX-TV|Fox 19]] |access-date=15 Apr 2020 }}</ref> On May 27, Cumberland announced he would return for his senior season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fox19.com/2019/05/27/ucs-cumberland-return-senior-season/ |title=UC's Jarron Cumberland to return for senior season |last=Danneman |first=Joe |date=27 May 2019 |website=fox19.com |publisher=[[WXIX-TV|Fox 19]] |access-date=15 Apr 2020 }}</ref>

Despite the deluge of transfers, Brannen was able to inspire a late-season recruiting renaissance, as he moved quickly to land Jeremiah Davenport, Chris Vogt, Mika Adams-Woods, Chris McNeal, Jaume Sorolla, and Jaevin Cumberland (in that order) - with the latter four commitments transpiring in under one week's time. It is worth noting that, at the time of the final scholarship being fulfilled, both Logan Johnson and Eliel Nsoseme were still in the transfer protocol and technically "could" return to UC; this series of signings effectively locked in their transfer from the program.

After all the dust settled, UC would have a final transfer enter the portal in redshirt Freshman LaQuill Hardnett. His spot would be filled shortly thereafter by the highest rated recruit of the 2019 class, Zach Harvey. Entering this season, new scholarship players would now outnumber returning players 7-6.

==Schedule and results==
The Bearcats traveled to in-state rival Ohio State to open the season for the second part of a home-and-home series with the Buckeyes. The Bearcats also began a home-and-home series with Tennessee beginning in the 2019–2020 season in Cincinnati. Tennessee visited Fifth Third Arena on December 18, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cincinnati to Start Men's Basketball Series with Tennessee |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2018/12/11/mens-basketball-cincinnati-to-play-home-and-home-basketball-series-with-tennessee.aspx |website=GoBearcats.com |access-date=2 April 2019}}</ref> The Bearcats traveled to Chicago to take on Iowa in the Chicago Legends event.<ref>{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball to Play Iowa in 2019 Chicago Legends Event |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2018/12/3/mens-basketball-to-play-iowa-in-2019-chicago-legends-event.aspx?path=mbball |website=GoBearcats.com |access-date=2 April 2019}}</ref> Cincinnati traveled to the Virgin Islands to compete in the [[Paradise Jam tournament]] where they finished in third-place.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cincinnati to Compete in 2019 Paradise Jam |url=https://gobearcats.com/news/2018/11/8/mens-basketball-cincinnati-to-compete-in-2019-paradise-jam.aspx?path=mbball |website=GoBearcats.com |access-date=2 April 2019}}</ref>
